title: Käthe Kollwitz's birth chart
metaDescription: Käthe Kollwitz's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 15.8° Cancer. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Tightest of all, the Sun holds a sextile to Pluto at 0.1° — close enough to weld identity to depth. Sextiles are read as standing invitations — productive exactly as often as they are accepted.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: At the noon reference the Sun sits 15.8° into Cancer — the second decan, which the old scheme hands to Mars. Same sign, different decan, different chart.

blocks.title: Closer to the ground
blocks.text: For the fast movers, Mercury was at 11.8° Leo, Venus was at 24.5° Gemini, Mars was at 9.4° Virgo. Read together: thought that arrives already in motion; attraction that begins as conversation; effort banked steadily until it tells.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Closest first: the Sun to Pluto, a sextile with 0.1° of slack. Sextiles are read as standing invitations — productive exactly as often as they are accepted. Behind it, Mars sextile Uranus at 0.4°, and the Sun square Neptune at 0.7° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. The unknown hour cannot unmake any of this: every aspect named survived all twenty-five samples of the day.

blocks.title: Figures in the geometry
blocks.text: Saturn opposes Pluto while both square Mercury. A t-square aims the whole axis at its apex planet; the tradition reads it as the chart’s standing assignment. Venus makes no major aspect that survives the day; the old reading gives such a planet autonomy — it acts alone, sometimes loudly.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The dignity table, which predates the outer planets and only ever spoke for seven, marks one placement here. Jupiter in Pisces at 7.3° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules. Dignity is a statement about conditions, not about worth.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: The honest balance sheet uses the 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day: water 4, air 2, fire 2, earth 2 across the elements, and cardinal 4, fixed 3, mutable 3 across the modalities. Water weights a chart toward the felt and the remembered — information that arrives as atmosphere before it arrives as words. Jupiter and Saturn were retrograde — the optical reversal the tradition reads as review — energy turned over before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Libra for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 12.8° between midnight and midnight. That is quick enough to make the exact degree a neighbourhood rather than an address, and slow enough to leave the sign settled. At the noon reference it stands at 12.3°.
